subject: RE: Payment for INV-2026-339 — escrow bridge or wire/ACH?
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@omnidata.com>

Cc: payments@omnidata.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payment for INV-2026-339 — scheduling wire or virtual card?

Hi Sofia,

We're ready to settle INV-2026-339 (PO-8891) but our procurement card payment kicked back at checkout. AP asked whether Redwood can accept a one-off wire or if you support virtual card/third-party escrow for this vendor payment. Total is $46,720.

Can you send:
- Wire instructions (bank + reference to include)
- Virtual card option or escrow partner contact (if available) and any fees that would apply
- Confirmation whether Redwood needs VAT documentation or a reverse-charge certificate — OmniData is US-based but the invoice shows VAT line and our tax team wants to reconcile.

We'd like to close this week if possible. Attaching PO-8891.

Thanks,
Alex Kim
Senior Accountant, OmniData
attachments: PO-8891.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@omnidata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:00:42 -0700
Subject: RE: Payment for INV-2026-339 — scheduling wire or virtual card?

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and for attaching the PO.

Options we can offer immediately:
1) Wire (fastest): use our bank stub attached (redwood_wire_instructions.txt). Please include reference INV-2026-339 and PO-8891 on the transfer so AP can match. Standard processing time after we receive funds is 1 business day.

2) Virtual card via our payments partner (no markup if charged by Friday 2026-10-02): we can route through our escrow partner and waive the processing fee for this transaction if you commit to the card charge by the end-of-week. I can generate the virtual card link if you confirm.

VAT/tax: since OmniData is US-registered, the VAT line on the invoice was included due to the provisioning region. If you can confirm your VAT ID or send a reverse-charge certificate, we will reissue a VAT-exempt invoice. If not, we can leave the invoice as-is but we need the remittance advice to show the VAT amount so our tax team can file correctly.

I'll ask Ben (cc'd) to monitor the receipt and prioritize reconciliation. I attached the official invoice (INV-2026-339.pdf) and our wire instructions.

Would you like the virtual card link or the wire today? If wiring, please send remittance proof (screenshot or confirmation number) once initiated.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | payments@redwood.com
attachments: INV-2026-339.pdf, redwood_wire_instructions.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:20:15 -0700
Subject: RE: Payment for INV-2026-339 — scheduling wire or virtual card?

Alex — looping in to make the settlement as frictionless as possible. A few practical notes: 
- If you wire, please use beneficiary name "Redwood Inference, Inc." and include reference "INV-2026-339 / PO-8891" in the payment reference field. Smaller banks sometimes truncate references — a copy of the transaction reference or a screenshot helps us reconcile faster.
- For wires under $50k we can clear and apply credit same-day once funds are received; above that we confirm next-business-day.
- If you choose virtual card, confirm today so Sofia can generate the token and we can waive the fee. Our payments partner will send a one-time card link to payments@omnidata.com.

If there's any internal procurement paperwork blocking the card, let me know and we can accept the wire.

Thanks — I'll keep an eye out for remittance confirmation.

Ben Carter
Collections Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@omnidata.com>

- Sending payment confirmation screenshot (attached) to this thread once the transaction posts.
